clauses.quote: Brownian follows from their updates. A checker or binding MUST NOT reintroduce the distinction as a declaration.
clauses.note: A variable's declared type is exactly one of unknown or parameter; ODE-state, observed and Brownian status are never read from a declaration.
clauses.concern: No diagnostic or observable test is given: it is unclear whether this means a loader must reject a legacy type such as "state", or only that binding APIs must not expose such a field, so it cannot be stated as an accept/reject property as written.

clauses.quote: If a `shape` is declared as well, its extents MUST equal the ranges' extents, and a mismatch is `array_shape_mismatch`.
clauses.note: When an unknown is defined by a faq over explicit inline ranges and also declares a shape, the declared extents equal the range extents, else array_shape_mismatch.

clauses.quote: The array MUST match the declared `shape` after metaparameter folding; a wrong extent, a wrong rank, or a ragged array (sibling axes of different lengths) is a **load-time error**
clauses.note: An inline array default is accepted only if its nesting is rectangular and equals the folded declared shape; otherwise load fails.
clauses.concern: No diagnostic code is named for this load-time error (contrast array_default_without_shape just below), so cross-binding agreement can only be on the verdict, not the code.

clauses.quote: so such a `default` MUST be rejected at load with the structural diagnostic `array_default_without_shape`, reported at the offending `default`. The rule covers both declared types and the variables of every inline subsystem. A binding MUST NOT resolve it by dropping the variable from scope or by substituting a number.
clauses.note: An array-valued default on a variable with no (or empty) shape, at any subsystem depth, is rejected with array_default_without_shape at that default's pointer.

clauses.quote: a scalar on a shaped variable MUST be materialized over the variable's whole declared grid
clauses.note: A scalar default on a shaped variable denotes the full-shape array with that value in every cell, so index(p, k) equals the scalar for every in-range k.

clauses.quote: Because the format declares two types, every binding MUST expose the same functions to recover the finer categories a solver needs.
clauses.note: ode_states, observed_unknowns and algebraic_unknowns partition the unknowns; brownian/discrete/sampled/constant partition the parameters; system_kind is the first of sde, pde, nonlinear, ode whose condition holds.
clauses.concern: The text claims the three unknown sets partition the unknowns, but nothing forbids one unknown being both under D(.,t) on one LHS and the bare LHS of another equation (it would be in ode_states and observed_unknowns), and an unknown that appears in no equation at all is put in algebraic_unknowns by the 'no equation names them on its LHS' wording even though nothing constrains it.

clauses.quote: A binding MUST reject such a document in validation and MUST refuse to build it.
clauses.note: Any equation whose LHS names a parameter (bare, indexed, inside a faq, scoped into a subsystem, or under D) makes the document invalid with equation_defines_parameter, at validation and at build.

clauses.quote: variable or metaparameter MUST be bound by a `faq` enclosing it on that left-hand side
clauses.note: A string subscript of an index on an equation LHS that names no variable or metaparameter is bound by an enclosing LHS faq or the RHS faq's output_idx; otherwise unbound_index_symbol.

clauses.quote: Every other bare-index definition of an observed MUST be refused with `indexed_definition_unsupported_form`, naming `V`, rather than run.
clauses.note: A bare index(V, k...) ~ rhs definition runs as V ~ rhs exactly when the listed conditions hold, and is otherwise refused with indexed_definition_unsupported_form naming V.
clauses.concern: The preceding text says the definition runs 'when all three hold' but then lists four conditions (the fourth being the rank check), so the set of forms this clause refuses is stated inconsistently.

clauses.quote: It is implicitly declared (§4.9.1): a checker MUST NOT report it as `undefined_variable` or `event_var_undeclared`.
clauses.note: The placeholder _var is never reported as undefined_variable or event_var_undeclared wherever an ODE state is legal.

clauses.quote: the mounted component's `tests` array MUST be **dropped at load**: it is not part of the mounting document, and a runner whose test target is that document MUST NOT run it.
clauses.note: Resolving a {ref} mount yields a component with no tests, so the mounting document's set of runnable tests contains only tests on components it declares itself.

clauses.quote: The array MUST match the variable's declared `shape` after metaparameter folding, and a mismatch (a wrong extent, a wrong rank, a ragged array) is a **load-time error**
clauses.note: An inline-array value in initial_conditions or parameter_overrides is accepted only if it is rectangular and equals the variable's folded shape.
clauses.concern: No diagnostic code is named for the mismatch, so the property can only fix the verdict.

clauses.quote: A scalar override of a shaped variable is therefore a value of that variable's full shape, and MUST be honoured on whatever channel the binding uses for that shape
clauses.note: A scalar override on a shaped variable sets every element of that variable to the scalar; it is never ignored.

clauses.quote: A binding MUST resolve each key against the flattened names by this precedence, stopping at the first rule that applies:
clauses.note: Override-key resolution is the function: exact flattened name, else the longest dotted suffix of the key that is a flattened name, else the unique flattened name having the key as a dotted suffix.

clauses.quote: Every leading segment dropped along the way MUST name a **component or subsystem the document declares**
clauses.note: Rule 2 resolves a key only if every leading segment it drops names a declared component or subsystem.
clauses.concern: Rule 2 says 'the longest such suffix wins' and separately that every dropped segment must be declared; it does not say whether, when the longest suffix's dropped prefix fails the check, a shorter suffix whose dropped prefix passes is tried or rule 2 fails outright.

clauses.quote: A key that reaches none of the three is **unrecognized** and MUST be rejected
clauses.note: A key that resolves under none of rules 1-3 is rejected.

clauses.quote: A conforming runtime MUST reject the run rather than ignore the key or pick a winner.
clauses.note: A run whose overrides contain an unresolvable key, an ambiguous key, or two keys resolving to one variable is rejected, never run.
clauses.concern: This sentence makes any variable that two keys both resolve to an error, but the paragraph after the table says an exact hit plus a rule-2/3 claim on the same variable is resolved silently in favour of the exact hit; the two statements disagree on that case.

clauses.quote: | Case | Condition | Diagnostic MUST |
clauses.note: The unknown-key diagnostic names the key; the ambiguous one names the key and every candidate; the colliding one names the variable and every colliding key.

clauses.quote: It MUST be distinguishable from the unknown case; binding one candidate arbitrarily is NOT conforming.
clauses.note: An ambiguous key yields a diagnostic class different from an unknown key and never binds any candidate.

clauses.quote: a validator MUST also reject an unknown key, with `unknown_override_key` at the key's pointer
clauses.note: A validator reports unknown_override_key at the escaped key pointer for every override key (element suffix stripped) matching no declared qualified name under rules 1-3, unless the document still holds an unresolved {ref} mount.

clauses.quote: A validator MUST reject an assertion whose `variable` is a bare name that the asserting component does not declare
clauses.note: An assertion whose bare variable (element suffix stripped) is not declared by its component is rejected with undefined_variable at the assertion's variable pointer; dotted names are not checked.

clauses.quote: A conforming runtime MUST use the symmetric scale; an asymmetric one is a divergence, not a rounding difference.
clauses.note: The tolerance test is |a - e| <= max(abs, rel * max(|a|, |e|)), symmetric in actual and expected.

clauses.quote: No `ε` floor is needed, and a conforming runtime MUST NOT introduce one
clauses.note: The pass predicate has no epsilon floor: for expected = 0 and abs = 0 a nonzero actual passes only if rel * |actual| >= |actual|.

clauses.quote: so only the infinite case needs the guard; a conforming runtime MUST apply it, and MUST NOT let any `abs` or `rel` bound admit a non-finite `actual`.
clauses.note: pass(a, e) = (a == e) or (a, e both finite and tolerance test holds); so a non-finite actual fails against every finite expected at every tolerance.
clauses.concern: The motivating claims are false as stated: not every IEEE-754 comparison with NaN is false (!= is true), and with rel = 0 the right side rel * inf is NaN, so the unguarded bound does not 'PASS for every expected value' (and max(abs, NaN) differs by language: Julia max propagates NaN, C fmax drops it).

clauses.quote: a runtime that accepts one MUST treat it as absent.
clauses.note: In per-field tolerance resolution a null abs or rel behaves exactly like a missing key.
clauses.concern: The same sentence says null 'is not conforming input', so a model must choose between rejecting it and treating it as absent; the clause permits both, so the verdict on a null tolerance is not determined.

clauses.quote: An assertion on a whole shaped field MUST select a scalar via either `coords` or `reduce`.
clauses.note: An assertion naming a shaped variable without an element suffix carries coords or reduce.

clauses.quote: Validators MUST reject, with `assertion_rank_mismatch` at the assertion's pointer
clauses.note: For a bare-name target, a pointwise assertion on a non-empty-shape variable (not an element name), or coords/reduce on a shapeless variable, is rejected with assertion_rank_mismatch.

clauses.quote: `coords` keys MUST match the spatial index-set names the field is shaped over.
clauses.note: Every coords key is one of the index-set names in the asserted variable's shape.
clauses.concern: No diagnostic code or rejection stage (validation vs run) is given for a coords key naming a set the field is not shaped over.

clauses.quote: conforming runtimes MUST implement exactly these):
clauses.note: Sampling uses idx = ceil(c - 1/2); integral is the mean over cells (unit measure per axis); from_file paths resolve relative to the .esm file's directory.

clauses.quote: The resolved index MUST lie in `1..size`.
clauses.note: ceil(c - 1/2) for each coords value lies in 1..size of its index set, else the assertion is invalid.
clauses.concern: No diagnostic code or stage is given for an out-of-range resolved index, and validators cannot always check it because index-set sizes may depend on metaparameters closed only at build.

clauses.quote: otherwise the assertion is ill-defined and validators MUST reject.
clauses.note: coords pinning a strict subset of the field's dimensions is rejected unless every unpinned dimension has size 1.
clauses.concern: The example ('a 1-D component with a single dimension') does not fit the rule: in a 1-D field a strict subset pins nothing, and the single remaining dimension resolves to one sample only if its size is 1; no diagnostic code is named either.

clauses.quote: Implementations MUST validate the shape and reject mismatches.
clauses.note: A from_file reference array is accepted only if its nesting equals the asserted field's shape.

clauses.quote: and it MUST read a parameter under the spelling that component's own **equations** use.
clauses.note: A build-time expression resolves a parameter name by flattened name, then owner-relative remainder, then a globally unique dotted suffix; any other name is unbound and an error.

clauses.quote: the flattened name stays authoritative and such an expression MUST qualify further
clauses.note: A suffix that is neither owner-relative nor globally unique binds nothing in the build-time scope.
clauses.concern: The clause says an ambiguous suffix 'binds nothing' and the expression must qualify further, but does not say whether this is a distinct error or falls under 'unbound', so the diagnostic for it is undetermined.

clauses.quote: The dimension names share that one scope with everything else in it, so a name MUST NOT be both.
clauses.note: An inline reference that mentions free a name that is both a dimension of the asserted field and already bound in the build-time scope (scalar parameters or build arrays, under any alias) is rejected naming the name.

clauses.quote: One name meaning two things in one scope is an ill-formed document, and an implementation MUST reject it with an error naming the clashing name
clauses.note: The clash is reported as an error naming the clashing name; neither meaning is chosen.

clauses.quote: An implementation MUST therefore reject a reference that mentions `t` free with an error naming it, rather than evaluating it.
clauses.note: An inline reference with a free t (not rebound by a faq and not a shape dimension) is rejected with an error naming t.

clauses.quote: Loading or validating such a document standalone therefore MUST NOT reject an index-set name it does not declare
clauses.note: Standalone load/validation of a component never reports undefined_index_set; an index-set name still unresolved after test injection is an error at build.
clauses.concern: 'Such a document' is not delimited: the clause reads as if every standalone document defers undefined_index_set, which would also stop catching genuine typos in components that are never injected.

clauses.quote: `y` names the variable plotted as a function of that dimension. Non-plotted spatial dimensions MUST be pinned in `pinned_coords`.
clauses.note: A field_slice plot has a pinned_coords entry for every spatial dimension of the field other than x.
clauses.concern: Since v0.8.0 (§6.3.1) the domain carries nothing spatial, so 'a domain spatial dimension' and 'more spatial dimensions than the plot uses' have no referent in the format.

clauses.quote: `value.variable` names the field. Non-plotted spatial dimensions MUST be pinned in `pinned_coords`.
clauses.note: A field_snapshot plot has a pinned_coords entry for every spatial dimension of the field other than x and y.
clauses.concern: Since v0.8.0 (§6.3.1) the domain carries nothing spatial, so 'a domain spatial dimension' and 'more spatial dimensions than the plot uses' have no referent in the format.

clauses.quote: for `field_slice` and `field_snapshot`, `x` MUST name a domain spatial dimension.
clauses.note: The x axis of a field plot names a spatial dimension of the plotted field.
clauses.concern: Since v0.8.0 (§6.3.1) the domain carries nothing spatial, so 'a domain spatial dimension' and 'more spatial dimensions than the plot uses' have no referent in the format.

clauses.quote: For `field_slice` and `field_snapshot`, `y` MUST be a single `PlotAxis` naming a domain spatial dimension.
clauses.note: The y axis of a field plot is a single PlotAxis.
clauses.concern: Contradicts the field_slice bullet just above and the §6.7.6 example, where y names the plotted variable (u), not a spatial dimension; only field_snapshot's y is a spatial dimension.

clauses.quote: If the underlying domain has more spatial dimensions than the plot uses, the extras MUST be pinned
clauses.note: Same as the field-plot pinning rule: every spatial dimension not on a plot axis has a pinned_coords entry.
clauses.concern: Since v0.8.0 (§6.3.1) the domain carries nothing spatial, so 'a domain spatial dimension' and 'more spatial dimensions than the plot uses' have no referent in the format.

clauses.quote: A binding that cannot honor the declared layout MUST reject the file at load rather than reinterpret bytes.
clauses.note: Binary byte-layout handling of data files is file I/O, not format semantics.

clauses.quote: it MUST refuse, naming the source, to build a provider for a source it was asked to build that has no `esio_format` and whose reader it cannot otherwise determine
clauses.note: Choosing an EarthSciIO reader in providers_from_document is runtime provider construction; the document itself is unaffected (esio_format is read nowhere by load, validation or flatten).

clauses.quote: it MUST NOT guess a reader for a source whose `esio_format` is present
clauses.note: Choosing an EarthSciIO reader in providers_from_document is runtime provider construction; the document itself is unaffected (esio_format is read nowhere by load, validation or flatten).

clauses.quote: is a load-time error, `data_source_url_unresolved`, whose message MUST name the offending data source and template.
clauses.note: A url_template or mirrors entry containing ${ fails at load with data_source_url_unresolved naming the source and the template.

clauses.quote: A source whose location cannot be resolved MUST fail with this diagnostic. It MUST NOT be skipped, and it MUST NOT be allowed to deliver an empty read or a consuming parameter's `default`
clauses.note: Location resolution is a total function to a file:// or scheme URL or the error data_source_url_unresolved; an error is never replaced by a skip, an empty read or a default.
clauses.concern: 'Cannot be resolved' is defined only by the ${ and ?/# cases; it is unclear whether a resolved URL whose file is missing at read time also falls under this diagnostic and its no-default rule.

clauses.quote: `update.source` MUST resolve to a `data_sources` key (`data_source_undefined` otherwise).
clauses.note: A data update whose source is not a key of data_sources is rejected with data_source_undefined.

clauses.quote: Its `size` MUST be 2 (after metaparameter folding, §9.7.6).
clauses.note: An index set carrying "records": true whose folded size is not 2 is rejected with record_axis_invalid at /index_sets/<name>.

clauses.quote: `temporal.records_per_sample`) MUST equal the number of records its record shape gives it.
clauses.note: A deprecated records_per_sample (the rule's own, else its source's) that differs from the count the record shape gives (2 when it begins with a record axis, else 1) is rejected with records_per_sample_invalid.

clauses.quote: A binding that validates before mounting refs MUST treat what a
clauses.note: Before refs are mounted, a param_to_var target behind an unmounted ref, and a record shape whose first entry is an index set the document does not declare while a ref remains unmounted, are skipped rather than judged; the reachable record shapes are still judged, and flatten checks the rest.

clauses.quote: and with none written the provider MUST refuse the parameter, naming it, rather than assume one record.
clauses.note: providers_from_document refuses a data-fed parameter whose record shape depends on a param_to_var target the given document does not show, when no deprecated value is written; a runtime provider concern, not a property of the document.

clauses.quote: reader does not recognise **MUST** be an error, not an ignored key
clauses.note: Reader option handling is file decoding, outside the format's semantics.
clauses.concern: Validity then depends on which format reader a binding binds, so the same document can be valid in one binding and invalid in another; no diagnostic code is named.

clauses.quote: applies it after the read is an optimization — the two **MUST** agree exactly.
clauses.note: Equivalence of reader pushdown and post-read selection is a data-access optimization contract.

clauses.quote: so a binding that does it MUST collect first and inline second.
clauses.note: The extent-name check accepts exactly the metaparameter names collected from the authored documents before any mount is inlined.

clauses.quote: *What counts as declared, and the two cases this check MUST NOT refuse.*
clauses.note: An extent metaparameter declared by the document, by a mounted document (transitively), or by an imported library and left unbound by the import edge is never reported as template_import_unknown_name.

clauses.quote: check is an AUTHORING check and MUST be idempotent
clauses.note: The extent check accepts a resolved document whenever it accepted the authored one: it is skipped when no {ref} mount remains and an index_sets entry has every interval size a concrete integer.
clauses.concern: The resolved-shape test is satisfied by an authored single file with literal integer index-set sizes and no mounts, so the misspelled-extent typo the preceding paragraph insists must stay caught escapes the check; 'at least one index_sets entry with every interval size' is also ambiguous about whether 'every' ranges over that entry or all entries.

clauses.quote: Bindings MUST NOT reject a zero or negative member.
clauses.note: Every integer (including 0 and negatives) is an acceptable enum member value.

clauses.quote: Within a single enum, integer values MUST be unique
clauses.note: Within one enum no two symbols map to the same integer.
clauses.concern: No diagnostic code is given for a duplicate value, and 'MAY NOT' in the same sentence is not an RFC 2119 keyword and can be read as a permission not to. Resolved 2026-10-26 (Q-8): MUST NOT, code enum_duplicate_value (spec.9.3.enum-duplicate-rejected).

clauses.quote: so two symbols MUST NOT both map to `0`. Bindings MUST reject an enum in which two symbols map to the same integer at load time with diagnostic `enum_duplicate_value`, whether or not any `enum` op names either symbol.
clauses.note: A document whose enums block has two symbols of one enum with the same integer (0 included) fails load with enum_duplicate_value, referenced or not.

clauses.quote: The `enum` op (§4.5) MUST resolve at load time, before any expression evaluation. After lowering, no `enum`-op nodes remain in the in-memory representation; each is replaced by a `{"op": "const", "value": <integer>}` node. Bindings MUST NOT propagate enum strings into evaluated expressions.
clauses.note: Enum lowering replaces each enum op by const of the integer its file's enums block assigns; the loaded tree contains no enum nodes.

clauses.quote: MUST be rejected at load time. Loading MUST fail.
clauses.note: An enum op naming an undeclared enum fails with unknown_enum, and an undeclared symbol with unknown_enum_symbol.
